messages:
Carla (Design): dropped a fresh Figma pass for the model catalog compare UI: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxx/new-compare-pass 
Carla (Design): main concerns: filter density on desktop, badge semantics (latency vs cost vs quality), and the version pin interaction on small screens
Ben (PM): nice. i like the tighter rows. question: should we hide advanced filters behind a chevron or keep them inline?
Maya (Product): analytics show advanced filters used ~9% of sessions, but they matter in comparison tasks. leaning progressive disclosure but obvious affordance
Dave (FE): hiding saves ~240px header width but adds keyboard focus traps. multi-select flows get slower behind a dropdown
Erin (A11y): dropdown ok if accessible. must be reachable in one tab stop and not trap focus. add skip link? also check focus order when panel opens
Carla (Design): proposal A: inline chips with compact wrap. Proposal B: "Show more filters" panel that expands below chips. Which is cleaner?
Alex (Design Eng): tech note: expanding panel is easier for animation and focus management. chips with wrap require complex row-height math on resize
Ben (PM): for badges: users misread color meaning in last test. Remove implicit color meaning, keep small numeric labels and a help tooltip
Maya (Product): agree. show p50 latency and an estimated cost metric. source both from last 24h rolling stats so numbers are comparable
Dave (FE): will need an endpoint for /catalog/stats?since=24h and caching on client-side. avoid firing for every row when 10 models on screen
Erin (A11y): badge text must be readable by screen readers. add aria-labels like: "Latency p50: 45 ms" and "Estimated cost per 1k tokens: $0.28"
Carla (Design): visual: small capsule badges inline under model title, not its own column. mobile: collapse badges under a single "i" affordance that opens a sheet
Ben (PM): mobile collapse makes sense. track clicks on badge, badge tooltip open rate, and misinterpretation in the study
Alex (Design Eng): about the pin: current pin icon sits isolated on row. idea: move pin next to version selector and make it a toggle with visible text on focus
Erin (A11y): hover-only reveal is a no-go. must be perceivable and operable via keyboard. use <button aria-pressed> and an sr-only label: "Pin this version for routing"
Carla (Design): agreed. also thinking of a brief inline confirmation after pinning: "Pinned v2.4 to route recommendations (undo)" that disappears after 5s
Maya (Product): add analytics event `catalog.version_pin` with props: model_id, version, route, user_role
Dave (FE): dev question: do we show exact p50 or a range? exact numbers fluctuate and might be noisy
Maya (Product): show p50 rounded to nearest ms + confidence band in tooltip. e.g., "p50: 48ms (24h median)" and tooltip: "Range 25-120ms"
Carla (Design): copy nits: change badge alt copy to shorter forms: "Latency (p50): 48ms" and "Cost/1k: $0.28". icons should have high contrast (WCAG AA)
Erin (A11y): contrast check: green lightning failed AA at small sizes. use darker fill or add outline for icon shapes. also ensure focus ring 3px for interactive capsules
Alex (Design Eng): implementation plan: initial MVP - inline badges + persistent pin next to version selector + expand/collapse advanced filters panel. will ship flags for A/B
Ben (PM): A/B variants: A = inline filters + badges visible, B = collapsed advanced filters + compact badges + pin on hover (for testing only). measure time-to-pin, filter usage, keyboard completion times
Dave (FE): pairing request: can Erin and I run keyboard + screen reader QA when i have the PR? I'll aim for Wed 10am PT
Erin (A11y): yes, i'll join and bring NVDA/VoiceOver checklist. also will run contrast validations and a11y tree checks
Carla (Design): i'll update Figma with the alternate flows and add notes about tooltip content and timing (200ms delay, 300ms to dismiss)
Maya (Product): i'll create the github ticket for the stats endpoint and tag infra for rate limiting. i'll also add the analytics tracking ticket
Ben (PM): thanks team. if no objections i'll add the dev spike to next sprint and schedule the A/B test ramp for the following week
Carla (Design): thanks everyone. quick thumbs if you're good with the direction :thumbsup:
